items.text:
This game released from Early Access (EA) into full release with very little content added from the beginning of EA.

There are very few ship parts, very little story, a handful of non-repeating quests, no uniqueness, nothing to explore. What you will see more than anything, is the hard-to-use build menu and the (spaceX) docking port.

In short, once you have finished your first salvage, you've experienced almost everything this game has to offer.

I could say more, but there is no reason to know more about this rather bareboned game, and that makes me sad.

这款游戏从抢先体验（EA）进入正式发布，相比EA初期几乎没有增加什么内容。

飞船部件极少，剧情极少，只有寥寥几个不重复的任务，没有独特性，没有什么可探索的。你看到最多的，就是那个难用的建造菜单和（SpaceX式的）对接端口。

简而言之，一旦你完成了第一次打捞，你就已经体验了这款游戏几乎所有的内容。

我还能说更多，但对于这款相当骨感的游戏，没有理由去了解更多，这让我感到难过。

items.text:
Edit: added parts about social and modding.

Full of bugs, poor design around every corner, and questionable balance. Also very unique, with absolutely no alternative.

Would I play it more? Absolutely. Would I enjoy it? Probably not. That's the nature of a toxic relationship.

Now, a little bit more in depth:

[h1]Bugs.[/h1]

There are a lot. Honestly, at some point I'm not entirely sure what is a bug and what is bad design. FPS drops, script errors, physics, memory leaks, everything would be broken at some point. I liked it a lot one time when the game created all files for a save, but didn't put them into a zip archive and couldn't read this save file. Easy fix, though.

[h1]Poor design[/h1]

Well, the list would be as long as the game features. Basically, everything that you would do in this game would be made in the most stupid, time-consuming, unfun way. I'm pretty sure that AI slop would make a better design. Here is a little list of examples:

When you load the game, the splash screen with update info is right before loading. I think it doesn't block the loading itself, it's just its placement is very inconvenient.

* UI is just plain bad. All of it. Like, when you're in a helmet, it blocks your UI. Because of this, I missed a very important button for 30 hours. All bags are just a fit of tedious micromanagement. Character traits are just a long list of perks without much formatting. Visor in damage mode doesn't let you see building marks, and it's VERY NEEDED to see them in that mode. When you dock, "Match speed" and "Prox Warn" alarms are not in the dock screen, AND YOU REALLY NEED THEM IN THE DOCK SCREEN.

* Quests are just 98% plain text, without barely any choices, no scene art, not even book formatting.
AI. It's very long to describe how poor the AI in this game is, it's easy to find info on all problems with it. Let's just say they often choose death instead of being part of this game. But without jokes, many people decide to play without crew at all and not deal with AI. I guess that says a lot.

* Close-quarters combat is rudimentary. Well, it's just not fun at its core and stupid. Why the hell do people with lethal wounds in vacuum die after like 5 minutes?

* Ship building. It mostly works. But there is absolutely no dry dock in the game, so you need to do it in vacuum, and that means you need to deal with AI and micromanage them, because they can randomly stop changing batteries or O2 tanks and just die. It's also a HUGE TIME SINK. At least 15 of my playtime hours were spent waiting for things to be done.

[h1]Loot[/h1]

It's sad to say, but you will see 80-90% of loot in the first 4 hours in the starter playground. There is just barely any WOW effect, not many things to be discovered. No gold mine to strike. It's just a tedious, steady grind. This problem is tied to general economy balance. In a game about making coin by salvage and exploration, this was a HUGE LETDOWN.

[H1]Social combat/NPC dialogues [/H1]

You know, I like it on paper. I think I even grasp what you need to do for results. But there is no real explanation of the system in the game or on the internet. But in reality, it's a mesh of bad UI and poor action feedback to the player. First, why do you need to look at 3-4 different parts of the screen to see the outcome of your actions after every click? Second, why do stats jump like mad when you click on an option with a simple outcome? NPCs 80% of the time answer gibberish because they play the same system, and you also say a lot of gibberish. There's really good gameplay here, but it's buried under layers of undercooked implementations.


[h1]Balance[/h1]

Well, it's shaky at best. Economy is weird and very artificial. As I said, it's a problem tied to loot. Without interesting, varied loot, it's hard to balance the economy. So they made GIGS. So you don't need to look for 10-20k ships, you can take a gig that will pay you 30k for a VERY easy task at the ship, and you can also loot this ship. But gig payments crumble under their own weight, because they're balanced around distance. So you have delivery gigs that pay you 1500, and the same delivery gigs that pay you 10mil. So, why would I salvage anything in this game about salvaging things, when I can just travel from A to B and make 2000% more profit?

Little bit about combat balance. Imagine, you're a skilled space suit user. You're in vacuum. You have a crowbar. You feel brave and on top of your game. You have no combat experience. And your enemy is a poor space suit user. He has insomnia and is on the edge of a breakdown. He's terrified. He has a pocket knife. He's 1 level higher than you in combat. Who would win? Of course, the enemy. He will absolutely destroy you with his bare hands; he wouldn't even use the pocket knife. I guess that's fair.

[h1]Mods[/h1]
Modding community is strong for a generally low playerbase. But they mostly fix annoying and bad design and UI, but they can't fix everything. This is a job for the developer. There really shouldn't be a mod that mutes the proximity alarm when you're docked, or a mod that adds EVA suit lockers, or a mod that lets AI grab multiple items before starting to work with said items. This all should be part of the base game like yesterday.

--------

So no, I can't recommend this game to anyone. Developers shouldn't release games in such a poor state out of desperation. But yes, I would probably play it more, because this is a way of a toxic relationship.
items.text_zh:
编辑：添加了关于社交和模组的部分。

到处都是bug，每个角落的设计都很糟糕，平衡性也值得怀疑。同时它又非常独特，完全没有替代品。

我会玩得更多吗？绝对会。我会享受它吗？大概不会。这就是有毒关系的本质。

现在，再深入一点：

[h1]Bug。[/h1]

有很多。老实说，到了某个时候，我都不完全确定什么是bug，什么是糟糕的设计。帧率下降、脚本错误、物理、内存泄漏，一切都会在某个时候出问题。有一次我特别喜欢的是，游戏为一个存档创建了所有文件，但没有把它们放进zip压缩包，然后无法读取这个存档文件。不过修复很简单。

[h1]糟糕的设计[/h1]

嗯，这个清单会和游戏功能一样长。基本上，你在这个游戏里做的每件事都会以最愚蠢、最耗时、最不好玩的方式来完成。我很确定AI生成的垃圾都能做出更好的设计。这里有一个小例子清单：

当你加载游戏时，带有更新信息的启动画面就在加载之前。我觉得它不会阻止加载本身，只是它的位置非常不方便。

* UI就是纯粹的糟糕。全部都是。比如，当你戴着头盔时，它会挡住你的UI。因为这个，我错过了30个小时里一个非常重要的按钮。所有背包都只是一堆繁琐的微观管理。角色特质只是一长串没有多少格式的perk。伤害模式下的面罩不让你看到建筑标记，而在那个模式下看到它们是非常必要的。当你停靠时，“匹配速度”和“接近警告”警报不在停靠界面里，而你在停靠界面里真的非常需要它们。

* 任务98%都是纯文本，几乎没有选择，没有场景美术，甚至没有书籍排版。
AI。描述这个游戏里的AI有多糟糕需要很长时间，很容易找到关于它所有问题的信息。我们就说他们经常选择死亡，而不是成为这个游戏的一部分。但不开玩笑地说，很多人决定完全不带船员玩，不跟AI打交道。我想这说明了很多。

* 近身战斗很简陋。嗯，它的核心就是不好玩而且愚蠢。为什么在真空中受了致命伤的人会在大概5分钟后死掉？

* 飞船建造。它基本上能用。但游戏里绝对没有干船坞，所以你需要在真空中进行，这意味着你需要处理AI并微观管理他们，因为他们会随机停止更换电池或氧气罐，然后直接死掉。这也是一个巨大的时间黑洞。我至少有15个小时的游戏时间花在等待事情完成上。

[h1]战利品[/h1]

说起来很遗憾，但你会在新手游乐场的前4个小时里看到80-90%的战利品。几乎没有什么WOW效果，没有多少东西可供发现。没有金矿可挖。这只是一个乏味、稳定的刷。这个问题与总体经济平衡有关。在一个通过打捞和探索赚钱的游戏中，这是一个巨大的失望。

[H1]社交战斗/NPC对话 [/H1]

你知道，理论上我喜欢它。我想我甚至明白你需要做什么才能得到结果。但游戏里或网上都没有对这个系统的真正解释。但实际上，它是糟糕UI和对玩家行动反馈不佳的混合体。首先，为什么你每次点击后都需要看屏幕上3-4个不同的部分才能看到你行动的结果？其次，为什么当你点击一个结果简单的选项时，属性会疯狂跳动？NPC有80%的时间回答的是胡言乱语，因为他们玩的是同一个系统，你也会说很多胡言乱语。这里确实有很好的玩法，但它被层层未煮熟的实现埋没了。


[h1]平衡[/h1]

嗯，往好了说也是摇摇欲坠。经济很奇怪而且非常人为。正如我所说，这是一个与战利品相关的问题。没有有趣、多样的战利品，就很难平衡经济。所以他们做了GIGS。这样你就不需要寻找1-2万的飞船，你可以接一个GIG，在飞船上做一个非常简单的任务就能付你3万，而且你还可以打捞这艘飞船。但GIG的报酬在自身重量下崩溃了，因为它们是围绕距离来平衡的。所以你有付你1500的送货GIG，也有付你1000万的同样的送货GIG。那么，在这个关于打捞东西的游戏中，我为什么要打捞任何东西，当我可以从A旅行到B并赚取多2000%的利润时？

关于战斗平衡说一点。想象一下，你是一个熟练的太空服使用者。你在真空中。你有一根撬棍。你感到勇敢，状态极佳。你没有战斗经验。而你的敌人是一个可怜的太空服使用者。他失眠，处于崩溃边缘。他吓坏了。他有一把袖珍刀。他在战斗中比你高1级。谁会赢？当然是敌人。他会赤手空拳绝对摧毁你；他甚至不会用袖珍刀。我想这很公平。

[h1]模组[/h1]
对于一个总体玩家基数很低的游戏来说，模组社区很强大。但他们大多修复烦人和糟糕的设计与UI，但他们不能修复一切。这是开发者的工作。真的不应该有一个模组来在你停靠时静音接近警报，或者一个模组来添加EVA服储物柜，或者一个模组让AI在开始处理物品之前抓取多个物品。所有这些昨天就应该成为基础游戏的一部分。

--------

所以不，我不能向任何人推荐这个游戏。开发者不应该出于绝望而发布处于如此糟糕状态的游戏。但是的，我可能会玩得更多，因为这是一种有毒关系的方式。

items.text:
Ostranauts is definitely not easy to recommend in its current state as of 1.0.  It's got jank and a lot of half-baked features, but the hard sci-fi elements of salvaging, building and piloting ships around the solar system is fun enough.  Traveling long distances feels equally rewarding and risky, as lack of preparation, improper planning or a piloting mistake will leave you stranded.  That said, you'll probably get a more complete experience if you wait a while for more patches to be added and mods to be developed.

Here a few things that I dislike about the current state of the game:

-NPC interactions.  I like the idea, but interacting with NPCs is just bland at the surface level once you understand the minigame.  There is hardly any unique dialogue outside of the rather few story missions.
-Speaking of missions, NPCs will randomly ask you, a seemingly complete stranger, to do a task for them that involves finding someone, talking to them (beating them up first being optional sometimes), and then traveling back.  The "someone to find" is random and sometimes on a completely different planetary body, or in my case, driving a police patrol craft in deep space 1.2 AU from Ganymede, where they should have been stationed.  Oh, and there is no reward for these, so I'm not really sure what the point is.  (The actual story missions are neat, but few and far between.)
-Lack of ship VFX.  We're under thrust using a torch drive burning at 4gs spinward, yet ships have no visible drive plumes.
-Stats of ship components are not visible anywhere.  For example, the mass and durability of walls and floors vary based on the manufacturer, but this isn't listed anywhere in-game and cannot be viewed outside of obtaining a mass scanner plugin for your PDA, which you probably won't find until you've already added on to your ship.  This applies to basically every electronic item in the game too.
-NPC crew member controls.  During scheduled work time, NPCs will often ignore orders and just do whatever the hell they want.  The only way I could get them to stop "studying" on the computer I installed in the break room was to unplug it during working hours.  Also there needs to be global orders you can quickly give that override other activities, such as "emergency repairs" and "secure for maneuvering" (to you know, get in a crash couch before they are crushed to death.)
-Lack of advanced hauling/bartering zone controls to let you specify exactly where items should be stored, and for NPCs to actually haul items to be stored there.  Currently, if I purchase scrap, it ends up in my fridge, even though the fridge is set as a "food only" zone.  The opposite happens too.  
-Physics simulation is a little too simple.  It doesn't matter where you put your thrusters or where your center of mass is, the ship behaves the same regardless.  Aerodynamics is determined entirely by mass and how many heavy lift rotors and aerodynamic hull parts you have, not necessarily the shape of the ship.  There is no explosive decompression, and atmospheric flight using heavy lift rotors needs a pass.  (Specifically, you have to have an even number of clockwise and counter-clockwise spinning heavy lift rotors, otherwise you get stuck in a death spin.  There is no way to change direction other than unpowering and repowering them.)
-Inventory is just weird.  You have a space suit, but no specially designed bag to carry stuff around in while in a space suit, so your character has to occupy a hand by dragging around a backpack permanently.
-No way to automate putting on/taking off a suit.  Until a person spends enough time in a space suit (upwards of a month from what I can tell), they suffer a severe work speed penalty.
-Lack of proper airlocks.  You're always briefly leaking atmos when crew enter/leave the ship because airlocks are effectively two doors put a few feet apart, with no way to "cycle" airlocks.
-Lack of crew retention and benefits.  Crew are paid a pathetic amount daily.  You could be bringing in millions in a trade run, but they're only getting $250.  Micromanage them too hard or don't meet one of their needs (which are somewhat obfuscated), and they'll just up and quit on you, and there is no way to give them a higher salary until they decide to quit.  A way to reward hard work (because crew do slack off)/match their pay to the skills they've developed since joining, and maybe even a healthcare plan to automate the treating those nasty blisters they got when your ship suddenly lost pressure and their skin boiled would be a really nice addition.

These are just to name a few, and thankfully, there are a few mods that can cover some half-baked features and IMO should be included in the full game:

"Ship's Water" - A mod that adds water tanks, showers, waste water storage/processing and the ability to bulk purchase water.  Otherwise, you're filling up bottles in slowly recharging sinks on stations, or tediously buying containers of it.  Crew need to drink and bathe with water with or without this mod, but this makes managing water much less tedious. This is seriously a "must have" mod.

"Uninstall and Haul" - In Vanilla, when you first dock with a wreck, you can run through and mark anything you want to salvage in-tact with an "uninstall" order.  Unfortunately, you will then have to order it to be "hauled" back to your ship after the component was uninstalled.  This mod adds a combined order that will save you a ton of time and needless tedium.
items.text_zh:
就1.0版本目前的状况而言，《Ostranauts》绝对不容易推荐。它有不少毛病和大量半生不熟的功能，但在太阳系各处打捞、建造和驾驶飞船这些硬科幻元素还是足够有趣的。长途旅行既让人感到有回报又充满风险，因为准备不足、计划不当或驾驶失误都会让你被困在途中。话虽如此，如果你等上一段时间，等更多补丁加入、模组开发出来，你可能会获得更完整的体验。

以下是我不喜欢游戏当前状态的一些地方：

-NPC互动。我喜欢这个想法，但一旦你理解了这个小游戏，与NPC互动在表面层面上就显得平淡无奇。除了相当少的故事任务之外，几乎没有任何独特的对话。
-说到任务，NPC会随机要求你——一个看似完全陌生的人——为他们做一项任务，包括找到某人、与他们交谈（有时可以先揍他们一顿，这是可选的），然后再返回。那个“要找的人”是随机的，有时在一个完全不同的行星体上，或者就我的情况而言，在距离木卫三1.2天文单位的深空中驾驶一艘警察巡逻艇，而他们本该驻扎在那里。哦，而且这些任务没有奖励，所以我真不太确定意义何在。（实际的故事任务很不错，但少而间隔很远。）
-缺乏飞船视觉特效。我们正在使用火炬驱动器以4g的加速度向旋进方向推进，但飞船却没有可见的驱动尾焰。
-飞船部件的属性在任何地方都看不到。例如，墙壁和地板的重量和耐久度因制造商而异，但这在游戏内任何地方都没有列出，除非为你的PDA获得一个质量扫描插件，否则无法查看，而你很可能在已经给飞船加建之后才会找到它。这基本上也适用于游戏中的每一件电子物品。
-NPC船员控制。在预定的工作时间，NPC经常会无视命令，想干什么就干什么。我唯一能让他们停止在我安装在休息室的电脑上“学习”的办法，就是在工作时间里拔掉电脑电源。此外还需要可以快速下达、覆盖其他活动的全局命令，比如“紧急维修”和“固定好准备机动”（你懂的，让他们在被压死之前坐进防撞座椅。）
-缺乏高级搬运/交易区域控制，无法让你精确指定物品应该存放在哪里，也无法让NPC真正把物品搬运到那里存放。目前，如果我购买废料，它最终会出现在我的冰箱里，即使冰箱被设置为“仅限食物”区域。反过来也会发生。
-物理模拟有点太简单了。你把推进器放在哪里、你的质心在哪里都无所谓，飞船的表现都一样。空气动力学完全由质量和你有多少重型升力旋翼以及空气动力学船体部件决定，而不一定是飞船的形状。没有爆炸性失压，使用重型升力旋翼的大气飞行也需要重新调整。（具体来说，你必须拥有偶数个顺时针和逆时针旋转的重型升力旋翼，否则你就会陷入死亡旋转。除了断电再重新通电之外，没有办法改变方向。）
-物品栏就是很奇怪。你有一套太空服，但没有专门设计的包可以在穿着太空服时携带东西，所以你的角色必须占用一只手，永久拖着一个背包。
只能永久拖着一个背包，占用一只手。
-无法自动穿上/脱下宇航服。在一个人在宇航服中待够足够长的时间之前（据我所知要一个月以上），他们会遭受严重的工作速度惩罚。
-缺乏真正的气闸。每当船员进出飞船时，你总是会短暂地泄漏大气，因为气闸实际上只是相隔几英尺的两扇门，无法对气闸进行“循环”。
-缺乏船员留存和福利。船员每天的报酬少得可怜。你可能在一次贸易运输中赚到数百万，但他们只拿到250美元。对他们微观管理得太狠，或者没有满足他们的某项需求（这些需求有些模糊不清），他们就会直接辞职不干，而且在他们决定辞职之前，你没有办法给他们更高的薪水。一种奖励辛勤工作（因为船员确实会偷懒）/让他们的薪酬与他们加入后发展出的技能相匹配的方式，甚至也许一个医疗计划来自动治疗当你的飞船突然失压、他们的皮肤沸腾时他们得到的那些讨厌的水泡，将会是非常棒的补充。

这些只是列举几个，幸运的是，有一些模组可以覆盖一些半成品功能，在我看来应该被纳入完整游戏中：

“Ship's Water”——一个添加水箱、淋浴、废水储存/处理以及批量购买水的能力的模组。否则，你只能在空间站上缓慢补水的洗手池里灌瓶子，或者繁琐地购买一箱箱的水。无论有没有这个模组，船员都需要用水喝水和洗澡，但这让管理水变得不那么繁琐。这绝对是一个“必备”模组。

“Uninstall and Haul”——在原版中，当你第一次与一艘残骸对接时，你可以跑过去并用“卸载”命令标记任何你想完好打捞的东西。不幸的是，在组件被卸载后，你还得再命令把它“搬运”回你的飞船。这个模组添加了一个组合命令，将为你节省大量时间和不必要的繁琐操作。

This is one of those really difficult reviews where I wish I could give a more nuanced rating than "yes" or "no", but I have to lean toward "no". While my hours are inflated (full hours get added up from if it was running when you enter/exit your computer's sleep mode), it's absolutely been something I'd come back to repeatedly, so if the question is "will you get ~$16  of entertainment?" the answer is very probably "Yes".

However, the game has MASSIVE flaws, and ultimately it hasn't changed much from the state it was in even like 4-5 years ago. 

I've seen a lot of reviews go into detail about issues with the AI, and while those can be real I think a lot of the discussion there is kinda missing the bigger picture:
[b]This game has no point.[/b]

Gameplay for you if you've started is gonna feel exciting! There's so many wrecks to go explore, if you have a keen eye you might notice a couple (as in just two...) nearby-ish areas worth checking out, and you'll probably find yourself in a pretty initially satisfying loop of scrapping ships for valuable components to sell and improving your own starter ship a little. 

Then you might start trying to flip ships to make some serious money sooner, or to at least be less dependent on OKLG since there's literally no sources of electrical power other than fusion reactors or buying it from a station.

Now the game will have started to feel a lot more grindy, especially as you start to realize how many systems just aren't deep at all... except maybe deeply repetitive. But alright, you're making money and maybe hired an NPC and you've been micromanaging twice as much as before because their autonomy sucks and the tools to give them specific orders suck (you can't even queue orders except in a very specific way that has no priority or order and might result in them deciding it's time to nearly smoke themselves to death in airlock instead of working). 

But hey, now you've got the cash to pay off your debt and afford fuel for the fusion reactor you've built by now! It's time to go torching across the system! And hey, there seemed to at least be one quest that had actual story to it instead of being FO4 infinite quest tier, over at The Flotilla, maybe the world's gonna finally open up now and have so much more depth!

Oh.

[i] Oh... [/i]

It's about here where, after journeying for a few days to Venus or Ceres, that feeling is going to start to creep in. You'll realize almost nothing is really different -- that every station feels exceptionally sterile and lifeless, and while there's a few tiny scattered bits of content you can try to participate in, there's somehow even less story content there to capture you than NEO Scavenger. 

Anyway, that probably does an adequate job of describing my main gripe with the game. 

Because, see, It runs well, it's truly cool how some systems can appear to have depth at first, and while there's massive issues with AI you don't really have to engage with them at all. Even with flaws like the AI, you can make some use of a crewmember by just keeping them on permanent repair duty inside the ship or just treat them as an organic sex doll + chatbot combo to keep your captain's moods up. Not that the moods really matter almost at all. 

Well, I guess even when saying it's cool, I can't avoid discussing flaws, huh! Same as I could discuss how cool the travel is... until you try docking at venus and realize the values you're provided are super wonky and there's very little in the way of orbital info provided to you, making docking a continuous-thrust sort of affair that somehow just feels deeply *wrong* speaking as a long-time player of games like KSP, COADE, Orbiter, etc.

Aaaaand then it always comes back to that sterility I mentioned. Every station feels empty and lifeless or just populated by ants, 99% of the apparent quests are totally sterile and literally lacking even distinct flavor text while the remainder aren't nearly common or deep enough and feel totally detached from all the systems you've otherwise been engaging with, and even the few legitimate additions compared to a few years ago like ship combat are just so simplistic and easy and hardly feel satisfying since they really don't feel meaningful on much of a level and tend to just make you realize that even on a systems level this is a game that might have 2 or 3 parts for something where another game might have 10 or 20+. 

Maybe some day Modders Will Fix It (tm), but I really don't think that seems likely. It's a great concept, but the execution is deeply lacking and frankly kinda lazy given the dev-time. If Dan ever reads this, I really don't wanna crush your spirits man, there's a reason I've still played the game probably something like 60-80 hours as of the time of the review, but this just feels like a game that could have been done significantly better instead of basically being released at a state that really feels like an Alpha or Beta build deeply in need of more content and depth. 




btw since some people have complained about performance, check my attached specs, my hardware absolutely isn't supercomputer tier and it runs just as well even on my thinkpad, I DO think the dev's done a pretty nice job on optimization.
items.text_zh:
这是一篇非常难写的评测，我希望能给出比“是”或“否”更细致的评分，但我不得不倾向于“否”。虽然我的游戏时长被夸大了（如果你在电脑进入/退出睡眠模式时游戏仍在运行，完整的小时数也会被累加进去），但这绝对是我会反复回来玩的东西，所以如果问题是“你能从中获得大约16美元的娱乐价值吗？”答案很可能是“能”。

然而，这款游戏有着巨大的缺陷，而且归根结底，它和四五年前的状态相比几乎没什么变化。

我看到很多评测详细讨论了AI的问题，虽然那些问题确实存在，但我认为很多相关讨论有点没抓住重点：
[b]这款游戏没有意义。[/b]

如果你刚开始玩，游戏体验会让你感到兴奋！有那么多残骸可以去探索，如果你眼尖的话，可能会注意到附近有那么几个（也就是仅仅两个……）值得一看的区域，而且你可能会发现自己陷入一个最初相当令人满足的循环：拆解飞船获取有价值的部件来出售，并稍微升级你自己的初始飞船。

然后你可能会开始尝试倒卖飞船来更快地赚大钱，或者至少减少对OKLG的依赖，因为除了聚变反应堆或从空间站购买之外， literally 没有任何电力来源。

现在游戏会开始感觉更加肝了，尤其是当你开始意识到有多少系统根本毫无深度……也许只是深度重复。但好吧，你在赚钱，也许雇了一个NPC，而且你一直在做双倍的微观管理，因为他们的自主性很糟糕，而且给他们下达具体命令的工具也很糟糕（你甚至无法排队命令，除非用一种非常特定的方式，这种方式没有优先级也没有顺序，可能导致他们决定是时候在气闸里把自己差点熏死，而不是去工作）。

但是嘿，现在你有现金来还清债务，并为你现在已经建好的聚变反应堆买得起燃料了！是时候穿越整个星系了！而且嘿，在The Flotilla那里似乎至少有一个任务有真正的剧情，而不是FO4那种无限任务级别的东西，也许世界终于要开放了，会有更多的深度！

哦。

[i] 哦…… [/i]

大约就是在这里，在前往金星或谷神星旅行了几天之后，那种感觉会开始悄悄袭来。你会意识到几乎没有什么真正不同——每个空间站都感觉异常 sterile 和毫无生气，虽然有一些零星的微小内容可以尝试参与，但那里能吸引你的剧情内容不知怎的比NEO Scavenger还要少。

总之，这大概足够描述我对这款游戏的主要不满之处了。

因为，你看，它运行良好，有些系统一开始看起来有深度，这真的很酷，而且虽然AI有巨大的问题，但你其实完全不必去碰它们。即使有AI这样的缺陷，你也可以通过让船员在飞船内永久执行维修任务来利用他们，或者干脆把他们当作有机性爱娃娃+聊天机器人的组合来保持船长的情绪。倒不是说情绪几乎完全不重要。

好吧，我想即使是在说它酷的时候，我也无法避免讨论缺陷，是吧！就像我可以讨论旅行有多酷……直到你尝试在金星对接，然后意识到提供给你的数值超级不稳定，而且几乎没有提供任何轨道信息，使得对接变成一种持续推力式的操作，作为一个长期玩KSP、COADE、Orbiter等游戏的玩家来说，这不知怎的就让人感觉深深*不对劲*。

然后一切又总是回到我提到的那种 sterile 感。每个空间站都感觉空荡荡、毫无生气，或者只是挤满了蚂蚁，99%的表面任务都完全 sterile，甚至字面上缺乏独特的风味文本，而剩下的那些又不够常见或不够有深度，感觉与你一直在互动的所有系统完全脱节，即使是相比几年前少数几个真正的添加内容，比如飞船战斗，也太过简单和容易，几乎不让人觉得满足，因为它们真的在大多数层面上感觉没什么意义，而且往往只会让你意识到，即使在系统层面上，这也是一款可能只有两三个部分的游戏，而另一款游戏可能有10个或20个以上。

也许有一天Modders Will Fix It（tm），但我真的不认为那看起来有可能。这是一个很棒的概念，但执行深度不足，坦率地说，考虑到开发时间，有点懒惰。如果Dan读到这个，我真的不想打击你的士气，老兄，我在写这篇评测时仍然玩了大概60到80个小时是有原因的，但这感觉就像是一款本可以做得明显更好的游戏，而不是基本上以一个真的感觉像是Alpha或Beta版本的状态发布，急需更多内容和深度。




顺便说一句，既然有些人抱怨性能问题，看看我附上的配置，我的硬件绝对不是超级计算机级别的，即使在我的ThinkPad上运行得也一样好，我确实认为开发者在优化方面做得相当不错。
在提供给你的轨道信息方面，对接变成了一种持续推力式的操作，作为一个长期玩KSP、COADE、Orbiter等游戏的玩家来说，这种感觉莫名地就是深深*不对劲*。

然后，一切又总是回到我提到的那种死气沉沉。每个空间站都感觉空荡荡、毫无生气，或者只是被一群蚂蚁占据着，99%的表面任务都完全死板，甚至字面上连独特的风味文本都没有，而剩下的那些又不够常见或不够深入，感觉与你本来一直在互动的所有系统完全脱节，即使是相比几年前少数几个真正的添加内容，比如舰船战斗，也太过简单、太容易，几乎感觉不到满足感，因为它们真的在大多数层面上感觉不到有意义，而且往往只会让你意识到，即使在系统层面上，这也是一个可能只有2到3个部分的东西，而另一个游戏可能会有10个或20多个。

也许有一天Modders Will Fix It (tm)，但我真的不认为那看起来可能。这是一个很棒的概念，但执行上严重不足，坦率地说，考虑到开发时间，还有点懒。如果Dan读到这个，我真的不想打击你的士气，老兄，有一个原因是我在写这篇评测时可能已经玩了大概60-80小时，但这感觉就像是一个本可以做得明显更好的游戏，而不是基本上以一个真的感觉像是Alpha或Beta版本的状态发布，急需更多内容和深度。




顺便说一句，既然有些人抱怨性能问题，看看我附上的配置，我的硬件绝对不是超级计算机级别的，即使在我的ThinkPad上运行得也一样好，我确实认为开发者在优化方面做得相当不错。

items.text:
One of my biggest discoveries this year. Same dev as Neo Scavenger, so expect an incredible atmosphere, god-tier writing, and an unforgiving yet incredibly satisfying gameplay loop.

You start as a shipbreaker trying to escape an inhumane, dead-end job that barely pays enough to survive. You take out a massive loan and buy what is basically a flying coffin that's falling apart before your eyes, all so you can finally start making your own choices in the harsh, unforgiving reality of the OKLG.

I still remember the first time I sold a big haul. After one crazy expedition that I somehow survived in one piece, I made more money than I had earned after years of grinding, sacrificing, and saving every dollar while working as another disposable megacorp employee. There's something incredibly compelling—almost relatable—about that feeling.

It's a space sim where you go from absolutely nothing to... maybe not a millionaire, but someone who took control of their own life and built the future they wanted. All of this takes place in a dystopian world where humanity has colonized the Solar System while simultaneously losing contact with Earth (Kessler Syndrome).

This is the good part—actually, the great part.

But then there's the second part.

I would summarize it in one sentence:

Lots of small, medium, big, or just game-breaking problems have been reported over the years, and they're still in the game. The devs know about them very well.

So what do they do?

Yep. They decide to ship 1.0 next month.

As a software engineer myself, it's just painful to watch.

Here's a short list of those problems:

- CTDs.
- Insane loading times (partially fixable with Nexus mods).
- Broken quests (people on Steam and Discord literally recommend not engaging with them).
- A UI that feels like it was designed to make you suffer.
- The game clearly wasn't designed around controlling more than one character, yet it pushes you hard to hire a crew. The AI is from hell, the UI somehow gets even worse, and this introduces all sorts of problems the devs simply didn't think through. The absolute king is below:
- And the worst part: horrible performance. At some point (mid to late game), it becomes literally unplayable. I'm not talking about the usual stuttering that's already everywhere. I'm talking about one frame every three seconds. Yes—0.33 FPS. Performance is such a well-known issue that it even has its own thread on official Discord server. You can reproduce it very easily: just queue around 20 commands (for example, dismantling ship hull walls) while having 4 or more NPCs. The lag persists even after cancelling those commands. Good luck saving the game or reloading it while running at one frame every three seconds. Kekw's on you.

Now look at this list of problems and ask yourself:

"Why. instead of fixing above. the devs are shipping new features that introduce even more bugs, and then set 1.0 release date for next month?"

¯\_(ツ)_/¯

If you still want to play it, here's one pro tip:

Don't hire NPCs. The game was clearly designed around playing a single character. You'll have a lot more fun that way, while minimizing negative-fun you are getting. Trust.
items.text_zh:
这是我今年最大的发现之一。和《Neo Scavenger》是同一个开发者，所以可以期待令人难以置信的氛围、神级的写作，以及一个毫不留情却又极其令人满足的游戏循环。

你一开始是一名拆船工，试图逃离一份不人道、没有前途、几乎不够糊口的工作。你贷了一大笔款，买了一艘基本上就是会飞的棺材、在你眼前分崩离析的船，只为了终于能在OKLG严酷无情的现实中开始做出自己的选择。

我仍然记得第一次卖掉一大批货物的时候。在一次我不知怎么毫发无伤地活下来的疯狂远征之后，我赚到的钱比我作为又一个可随意丢弃的巨型企业员工，多年苦熬、牺牲、省下每一块钱所赚到的还要多。那种感觉有一种难以置信的吸引力——几乎让人感同身受。

这是一款太空模拟游戏，你从一无所有到……也许不是百万富翁，但成为一个掌控了自己人生、建立了自己想要未来的人。这一切都发生在一个反乌托邦世界里，人类已经殖民了太阳系，同时却与地球失去了联系（凯斯勒综合征）。

这是好的部分——其实，是极好的部分。

但接着还有第二部分。

我会用一句话来总结：

多年来人们报告了大量小的、中等的、大的，或者干脆就是破坏游戏的问题，而它们仍然留在游戏里。开发者们对此非常清楚。

那他们怎么做？

没错。他们决定下个月发布1.0。

作为一名软件工程师，看着实在令人痛苦。

以下是这些问题的一小部分清单：

- 崩溃到桌面。
- 疯狂的加载时间（用Nexus的模组可以部分修复）。
- 损坏的任务（Steam和Discord上的人真的建议不要碰它们）。
- 一个感觉像是专门设计来让你受罪的UI。
- 这款游戏显然不是围绕控制多个角色设计的，却硬是逼着你雇佣船员。AI来自地狱，UI不知怎么变得更糟，还引入了开发者根本没想清楚的各种问题。绝对的王者在下面：

Games like Ostranauts make me hate Early Access.

I was really excited about this game when it came out. A hobo simulator from the creator of NEO Scavenger, only now in space? Being able to create, modify and dismantle ships in an open world sandbox where other space hobos went about their day, blazing your path through the galaxy, all in a systems-intensive, survival sim where taking care of your ship is as important as taking care of yourself?! Sign me the hell up! Okay, sure, it's in a bit of a rough shape right now, but it just came out on Early Access, I'm sure with time things will improve.

And one year passed by. Two. Three. Six years Ostranauts has permanently been installed in my computer, always taking a peek after a major update, and always bouncing off hard due to very frustrating, elemental jank that would force enormous rollbacks to my save. Confusing UI; brain-dead AI getting into looping, nonsensical conversations; unintuitive objectives relying on poorly explained unique interactions. Over the span of months the developers would keep futzing around, fleshing out one ancillary feature while introducing 5 more bugs and while the rest of the core loop would remain a raging dumpster fire: AI ships colliding because they couldn't figure out the way to dock, NPCs acting completely randomly, entire stations decompressing, broken pathing... game breaking ♥♥♥♥ would keep getting pushed to the main version, and slowly but surely, reality started to set in: the game wasn't going to grow, we'd be lucky if the developers ended up making it playable.

Ostranauts has barely developed through Early Access. It entered as barely an alpha, and it's leaving barely a beta. The only thing Blue Bottle Games has managed to do in this time is add fluff like missions full of scripting errors and vague, blink-and-you'll-miss objectives that you will never again be able to track once that dialog box closes, and even if we ignore the still very real colossal ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ that can absolutely brick your game unless you roll back 30 minutes worth of progression, the core game loop is just not fun, because it's barely developed from the almost placeholder gameplay from 2020. Every single feature feels as ugly, unintuitive and ungainly as the gameplay itself.

The game still feels like there's a ton of progression that either was never intended to be there, or that the developers gave up on. The difference between "space hobo" and "actually pretty well off" is minimal, as itemization usually boils down to "you have nothing" or "you have the best tool in the game because there's only one". Maybe you'll get a second, middle option if you're lucky (as in, you may have no screwdriver, a normal screwdriver or an *electric* screwdriver). You can still collect all kinds of trash and put them in containers, boxes and bins, but since there's no crafting, you don't really have a reason to do so and it becomes incredibly tedious to browse through which bin has the bag that has the jacket that has your food. What worked in NEO scavenger to make you feel resourceful and crafty becomes bloated and purposeless in Ostranauts.

The mechanical tinkering and systems management which was once one of the most exciting prospects when the game came out is for the most part reduced to a few increasingly flashy flavors of "on or off". There's no logic, no programming, no deeper interactions than "connect air pump to air sensor". Expanding your ship feels unsatisfying and clunky, mostly due to the godawful UI. Okay, let me put an example:

Let's say you want to move 5 units of cable. You can't queue up orders, instead, what you want to do is:

- Click your PDA
- Click on "orders"
- Click on "uninstall"
- Unselect all the options except "conduit" (otherwise you're going to uninstall the floor)
- Drag a square through those 5 units
- Set your character on "autotask"
- Wait for them to uninstall the 5 units of cable
- Pick up the cable (otherwise your character is going to pick each piece individually)
- Select "install" (not "orders" you silly goose!)
- Scroll down a list of every single item in the game (yes, that includes every single variant of floor and wall, regardless of whether it's in your inventory or vicinity) until you find the exact thing you want to install.
- Set down the work order for each item you want to install
- Set your character on "autotask"
- Wait for them to do the job.

The alternative is to right click on each piece of cable, select "uninstall", and wait for the character to uninstall the bit of cable before being able to right click on the next one, being very careful that each of those right clicks actually selects the cable, otherwise you might uninstall the floor and completely vent your ship to space. Oops! Hope you saved not too long ago!

Taking care of your character is similarly a thankless, overwrought chore, with a billion little interactions that will keep slightly tweaking up or down a million sub-needs like "intimacy" or "self worth", none of which ever really amount to anything. You will never make meaningful connections with NPCs because interactions amount to little more than Sims-like random topic exchanges lacking even a tiny bit of flavor text to make conversations feel real; and with quests being sterile, incredibly basic "this guy asks you to find this other guy and talk to him" affairs that require chasing down NPCs that will keep spazzing all over the place while trying to talk to them, Ostranauts fails feel alive or immersive. It fails to be a survival game, a sandbox game, an RPG, a builder, or a narrative adventure. It fails at everything. It is astonishingly bad, moreso when considering that its predecessor, NEO Scavenger, did actually a really good job when it came to progression, survival, and questing. It's just a loose collection of rough mechanics that never feel fun by themselves and never play into each other, controlled by a redundant, clunky, annoying UI that calling "undercooked" would be a kindness to.

For years I've kept hoping Ostranauts would actually develop in the direction it aimed for when it released, and yet it's going to "release" in what could barely be qualified as acceptable by the standards it itself set six years ago. It is a hollowed husk of potential ruined by a developer that has just been faffing around solving problems of their own creation instead of actually developing the game. It is a colossal disappointment, and a game that I'm truly sad to advise against.

Play NEO Scavenger instead. It's a bit of a rough gem with a lot of questionable design choices that really really likes to screw the player over, but it just does everything Ostranauts tries to do but better. If you want a mechanically deep, complex survival game, then play Stationeers instead. Want something snappier and less involved? Hardspace Shipbreaker. If you want a procedural, detailed world with hints of survival, Qud or Dwarf Fortress are good options.

Do not buy this game. Even if worked like it should (which it doesn't), and even if it was fun (which it isn't), it's just an incredibly shallow, unsatisfying, frustrating mess of a game. 3/10.

像《Ostranauts》这样的游戏让我痛恨抢先体验。

这款游戏刚出来的时候我真的很兴奋。一个由《NEO Scavenger》创作者打造的流浪汉模拟器，只不过这次是在太空里？能够在一个开放世界沙盒中创建、改装和拆解飞船，其他太空流浪汉也各自过着自己的日子，你在银河系中开辟自己的道路，这一切都发生在一个系统密集的生存模拟中，照顾你的飞船和照顾你自己一样重要？！算我一个！好吧，当然，它现在状态有点粗糙，但它才刚进入抢先体验，我相信随着时间推移情况会改善的。

然后一年过去了。两年。三年。六年了，《Ostranauts》一直永久安装在我的电脑里，每次大更新后我都会瞄一眼，然后总是被极其令人沮丧的、根本性的毛病狠狠劝退，这些毛病会迫使我大幅回滚存档。令人困惑的UI；脑死亡的AI陷入循环的、毫无意义的对话；依赖解释不清的独特交互的不直观目标。在数月的时间里，开发者们一直在瞎折腾，充实一个附属功能的同时引入5个新bug，而核心循环的其余部分仍然是一团熊熊燃烧的垃圾箱大火：AI飞船因为搞不清对接方式而相撞，NPC行为完全随机，整个空间站失压，寻路损坏……破坏游戏的♥♥♥♥不断被推送到主版本，慢慢地但确凿地，现实开始显现：这游戏不会成长了，如果开发者最终能让它变得可玩，我们就该谢天谢地了。

《Ostranauts》在抢先体验期间几乎没有发展。它进入时勉强算个alpha，离开时勉强算个beta。Blue Bottle Games在这段时间里唯一做到的就是添加一些填充内容，比如充满脚本错误的任务，以及模糊的、眨眼就会错过的目标，一旦那个对话框关闭你就再也无法追踪它们，而且即使我们忽略那些仍然非常真实的、巨大的♥♥♥♥♥♥♥——除非你回滚30分钟的进度，否则它绝对能让你的游戏彻底报废——核心游戏循环就是不好玩，因为它从2020年几乎占位符式的玩法以来几乎没有发展。每一个功能都像玩法本身一样丑陋、不直观、笨拙。

这游戏仍然感觉有大量进程要么从来就没打算存在，要么开发者已经放弃了。"太空流浪汉"和"其实过得挺不错"之间的差别微乎其微，因为物品化通常归结为"你什么都没有"或者"你拥有游戏里最好的工具，因为只有这一个"。如果你运气好，也许会有第二个中间选项（也就是说，你可能没有螺丝刀、有一把普通螺丝刀，或者有一把*电动*螺丝刀）。你仍然可以收集各种垃圾并把它们放进容器、箱子和垃圾桶里，但既然没有制作系统，你其实没有理由这么做，而且翻找哪个垃圾桶里有那个装着那件夹克的包、而那件夹克里又有你的食物，会变得极其繁琐。在《NEO Scavenger》中让你感到足智多谋、心灵手巧的东西，在《Ostranauts》中变得臃肿且毫无目的。

机械修修补补和系统管理，曾经是游戏刚出来时最令人兴奋的前景之一，如今在很大程度上被简化为几种越来越花哨的"开或关"。没有逻辑，没有编程，没有比"把气泵连接到空气传感器"更深入的交互。扩展你的飞船感觉不令人满意且笨拙，主要是因为那糟糕透顶的UI。好吧，让我举个例子：

假设你想移动5单位电缆。你不能排队下达命令，相反，你要做的是：

- 点击你的PDA
- 点击"订单"
- 点击"卸载"
- 取消选择除"导管"以外的所有选项（否则你会把地板也卸载掉）
- 拖一个方框框住那5单位
- 把你的角色设置为"自动任务"
- 等他们卸载那5单位电缆
- 捡起电缆（否则你的角色会一根一根地捡）
- 选择"安装"（不是"订单"，你这个傻瓜！）
- 向下滚动游戏里每一个物品的列表（是的，包括地板和墙壁的每一种变体，不管它是在你的库存里还是在附近）直到找到你想安装的那个确切东西。
- 为你想要安装的每个物品设置工作订单
- 把你的角色设置为"自动任务"
- 等他们完成工作。

另一种选择是右键点击每一段电缆，选择"卸载"，等角色卸载完那段电缆后才能右键点击下一段，同时要非常小心每一次右键点击确实选中了电缆，否则你可能会卸载地板，让你的飞船完全向太空泄压。哎呀！希望你不久前刚存过档！

照顾你的角色同样是一件吃力不讨好的、过度繁重的苦差事，有无数琐碎的交互会不断微调上百万个子需求，比如"亲密感"或"自我价值"，而这些需求从来都不会真正带来任何结果。你永远不会和NPC建立有意义的联系，因为交互不过是类似《模拟人生》的随机话题交换，连一丁点让对话显得真实的调味文本都没有；而任务则是干巴巴的、极其基本的"这个人让你去找另一个人并和他说话"之类的事，需要你追着那些在你想和他们说话时不停抽搐乱动的NPC跑，《Ostranauts》既无法让人感到鲜活，也无法让人沉浸。它作为生存游戏、沙盒游戏、RPG、建造游戏或叙事冒险都失败了。它什么都失败。它糟糕得令人震惊，尤其是考虑到它的前作《NEO Scavenger》在进程、生存和任务方面实际上做得非常好。它只是一堆松散拼凑的粗糙机制，本身从不让人觉得有趣，也从不相互配合，由一个冗余、笨拙、烦人的UI操控，说它"欠火候"都算是客气了。

多年来我一直希望《Ostranauts》能真正朝着它发布时所瞄准的方向发展，然而它即将以按照它自己六年前设定的标准都勉强算合格的状态"发布"。它是一个被掏空的潜力躯壳，被一个只是一直在瞎忙活、解决自己制造的问题而不是真正开发游戏的开发者毁掉了。这是一个巨大的失望，也是一款我真的很遗憾要劝人别买的游戏。

去玩《NEO Scavenger》吧。它是一颗有点粗糙的宝石，有很多可疑的设计选择，非常非常喜欢坑玩家，但它就是把《Ostranauts》试图做的一切都做得更好。如果你想要一个机制深刻、复杂的生存游戏，那就去玩《Stationeers》。想要更爽快、更轻松的？《Hardspace Shipbreaker》。如果你想要一个程序生成的、细节丰富的、带点生存元素的世界，《Qud》或《Dwarf Fortress》都是不错的选择。

不要买这个游戏。即使它像应该的那样运作（但它并没有），即使它好玩（但它并不好玩），它也只是一款极其肤浅、令人不满、令人沮丧的烂游戏。3/10。

[h2]Don't buy it, the project is abandoned[/h2]

The game was released for purchase in 2020. Let's see what we get after 6 years:
- Updates once every 2-3 months
- We can do a whole [b]TWO[/b] (!) types of quests:
-- Fly to inspect a corpse (just an action "inspect corpse")
-- Fly and talk to a person (different forms, but the essence is always the same – fly over and interact with some person)
- We can talk to people, but it's pointless, because those we're friends with are no different from strangers
- We have a whole [b]TWO[/b] (!) stations, even though there are tons of them on the map – fly there and you'll find nothing but empty drafts, which is a consequence of the next point
- The whole world has about [b]FIFTY[/b] NPCs (lol), who differ only by name
- We can… Uh… do cargo logistics between the main station and the dummy stations, but it's not clear why: the profit, after fuel costs, is less than taking corpse inspection jobs.

So the game is completely empty. This [i]would[/i] be a great start for a game, but the game has been out for [b]SIX[/b] years. There's simply nothing to do – [b]absolutely nothing[/b]. Beyond 2000km from the starting zone (a couple minutes of flight) there's nothing – it's just an illusion of space. Literally the same as No Man's Sky – a wonderful illusion of a big world, but behind the decorations it's completely empty.

For six years of development, the game looks completely abandoned – an eternal demo version.

[h2]别买，这个项目已被放弃[/h2]

这款游戏于2020年开放购买。让我们看看6年后我们得到了什么：
- 每2-3个月更新一次
- 我们可以做整整[b]两[/b]（！）种任务：
-- 飞过去检查一具尸体（只是一个“检查尸体”的动作）
-- 飞过去和一个人交谈（形式不同，但本质始终一样——飞过去和某个人互动）
- 我们可以和人交谈，但这毫无意义，因为那些和我们成为朋友的人和陌生人毫无区别
- 我们有整整[b]两[/b]（！）个空间站，尽管地图上有成吨的空间站——飞过去你会发现除了空荡荡的草图什么都没有，这是下一点的后果

The game has a lot of potential but it's still very raw. I'd wait for the 1.0 release and then probably wait some more.

Pros: Has a really neat hands-on ship building mechanic, you can either buy or use the scavenge from derelicts to continuously build up your ship by increasing it's size and adding on more components such as thrusters, batteries and atmosphere control. Because of this and the money you get from selling scavenge that you don't want or need, there's a decent feeling of progression. Character creation is pretty in-depth with characters having many possible stats and perks including npcs. The low fidelity graphics are decently charming and the OST really adds to the dystopian vibe of the game. There's also a decent attempt at world building with the in-game manuals and occasional lore that's shown to you when you get to new locations for the first time.

Cons: Horribly clunky UI with very little quality of life, you'll struggle with it a lot and it really becomes frustrating after a while, and it only gets worse as you try to assign multiple orders to either dismantle and haul scavenge back to your ship, or assign orders to construct walls, floors and equipment all while dealing with your crew's AI. Imagine a MUCH less efficient and hard to use Rimworld UI (and AI) and you'll have an idea of what it's like.

Despite the attempt at worldbuilding, the world itself feels very dead. Locations which are implied to be massive end up being a small and barren collection of boxes and corridors, such as a "flotilla" of supposedly countless ships welded together that serve as the backbone of crime and freedom fighters of the system that ends up being just a few rooms with only a handful of npcs.

There also doesn't seem to be any dialogue whatsoever, character interactions are done through generic prompts such as "reassure" or "complain about authority", which help increase or decrease the character's various social needs. It's the same thing for quests, you'll regularly be contacted by npcs to do various tasks which all tend to be either to bring them something or to talk to another npc with just one or two prompts, these all also have very short introduction and completion texts, and they make you wonder why you even did them to begin with. All of this adds to the feeling of emptiness of the world.

Bugs are very frequent and often involve the AI, such as npcs walking through walls or spawning outside stations and suffocating to death, running into walls perpetually or getting stuck in airlocks, not following commands and refusing to look after their own needs.

I have a lot more nitpicks towards the game, but I hope this is enough to give you an idea of what to expect.

这款游戏潜力很大，但目前还非常粗糙。我会等到1.0正式发布，然后可能还要再等一阵子。

优点：有一个非常精巧的亲手造船机制，你可以购买或利用从废弃飞船中打捞来的材料，通过增大飞船尺寸并添加推进器、电池和大气控制等更多组件来不断升级你的飞船。正因如此，再加上出售你不需要或不想要的打捞物所获得的钱，有一种不错的成长感。角色创建相当深入，角色拥有许多可能的属性和特长，包括NPC。低画质的图形颇有魅力，原声带确实增强了游戏的反乌托邦氛围。游戏还通过内置手册以及你首次到达新地点时偶尔展示的零散背景故事，对世界观构建做出了不错的尝试。

缺点：UI极其笨拙，几乎没有便利性功能，你会为此挣扎很久，过一阵子真的会变得令人沮丧，而且当你试图分配多个命令去拆解并把打捞物运回你的飞船，或者分配命令建造墙壁、地板和设备，同时还要应付你船员的AI时，情况只会更糟。想象一个效率低得多、难用得多的《环世界》UI（以及AI），你就能大致明白是什么感觉了。

尽管尝试了世界观构建，这个世界本身却感觉非常死气沉沉。那些暗示规模庞大的地点，最终不过是些小而荒芜的箱子和走廊的集合，比如一支据说由无数飞船焊接在一起、作为该星系犯罪与自由战士支柱的“舰队”，结果只是几个房间和寥寥几个NPC。

而且似乎完全没有任何对话，角色互动都是通过诸如“安慰”或“抱怨权威”之类的通用提示来完成的，这些提示有助于增加或减少角色各种社交需求。任务也是一样，你会经常被NPC联系去做各种任务，而这些任务往往要么是给他们带点东西，要么是跟另一个NPC说话，只有一两个提示，这些任务也都有非常简短的介绍和完成文本，让你不禁怀疑自己当初为什么要做它们。所有这些都加剧了世界的空虚感。

Bug非常频繁，而且常常涉及AI，比如NPC穿墙行走，或者在空间站外生成后窒息而死，永远撞墙，或者卡在气闸里，不服从命令，拒绝照顾自己的需求。

我对这款游戏还有更多吹毛求疵的地方，但我希望这足以让你了解可以期待什么。

I'm nearly at a 100 hours and I'm having a good time. You'll start rough and you'll go through a couple characters if you don't go get a meta build from YT or reddit and you'll struggle a bit to figure out some of the mechanics. But after accidentally spacing yourself, slamming into an asteroid or running out of fuel you'll realize what stuff is worth scavenging, you'll make some money and buy and EVA suit. Then the world is yours and I'm hearing whispers of a mystery but haven't seen anything yet. If you enjoy managing your character and puzzling out why your ship is struggling and find pride in making it purr you'll have a good time.

A few cons (keep in mind it is early access): I'm unsure what causes it but there are some frequent freezes sometimes, I have abandoned some sessions because it was frequent and got frustrating. Usually a restart stops it and some days I'll play for 10 hours straight and never see a freeze. Most common for me at the main station.
 I wish there was more incentive to do the quests beyond making enough money for your first license. 
I wish there was a bit more to do with the NPCS and the stations in general, the loop of scavenge, sell, scavenge, expand, scavenge, sell can get a little boring. 
I really like the character creator but I wish there was better explanation of how to pick up some of the missing skills in game so that you could have more variety in the character. Because I delete the save if my character dies I end up with quite a few characters with the similar skills.

Edit: tried it again Sept 16, 2026. Just give me my ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ money back. I couldn't get through the tutorial. Where is the "Nav station"? What do any of the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ starting traits even DO? Why am I clicking on any of these ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ things? What an utter piece of ♥♥♥♥ this "game" is.....


The short version: this game is a janky, broken mess that screams out for a quality-of-life pass. I deeply regret buying it, and a significant portion of my 16hrs of playtime were spent redoing things that broke, or just trying to figure out some very basic things. It's bad. Avoid.

Longer version: I love Hardspace: Shipbreaker. I love games where you can salvage and build. The salvaging and building part of the game is... fine. It functions. You can right click on a thing, click "uninstall", and your character uninstalls it. You can right-click a thing, click on "repair" or "restore" and they do that. You need a variety of tools to do these things, and some of them need power. Cool. All of this is great.

And then the wall of your (broken down) ship breaks due to wear and tear, and you need to repair it. Awesome! Some urgency! But... You can't repair the wall cause the cooler is in the way. Fine, fine, I'll just uninstall the cooler: done. Repair the wall? Easy. I'll just put the cooler back now... Oh... I can't install the cooler? In the spot where it just was? But... It was just there?

The placement grid is all translucent grey, so that means there's nothing in the way... But, of course, there can't be anything in the way because how else could the cooler have been where it was? How could I have uninstalled it if there were things in the way. Maybe I need to be able to access the outside of my ship?

A long, long time passes while I figure out how to safely access the outside of my ship: nope, still can't install the cooler.

Turns out that if you really, REALLY zoom all the ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ way in, the corners of one of the placement squares *around* the cooler (note: not the cooler itself) is a very mild tinge of pink. Meaning there's an N2 canister in the way. But if the N2 canister is in the way of the install, how the ♥♥♥♥ did I UNinstall the cooler?

There are several times where I intentionally "dropped" a dolly (essentially a large shopping cart) and coudn't pick it back up. Why? Who ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ knows, the game sure isn't telling me.

If you drag a component you have legitimately salvaged into the station and start dismantling it in the public space, security will rush over and arrest you. Why? It's a ♥♥♥♥♥♥♥ mystery.

How does Character creation work? What do the choices *mean* in the context of the game? What does "skilled" mean? If I'm "5% training" in a skill, how much does the skill increase per relevant skill use? Also: what the ♥♥♥♥ do these skills enable? What do they DO? What do I need them for? In what way are they relevant? Why did dismantling a sleeping bag increase my ***structural engineering*** skill, ffs?

This is in addition to broken quests, and irrelevant things that just don't make any sense. For example, I received an SOS from an NPC ship who wanted fuel. Sure, sez I, and zipped over as quick as I could.
Me: "I'm requesting docking"
NPC: "♥♥♥♥ you, back off"

Um... What? The transponder call-sign matched the ship, but... They just preferred to drift in space.

You get random quest pop-ups: Some dude calls you and wants to talk, you should find and speak to him.
Me: Cool. Where is he.
Game: *shrug*
Me: ok, but he called me and asked to meet. Did he give me a ship name?
Game: *shrug*
Me: is he on this station?
Game: Nope.
Me: So....?
Game: ♥♥♥♥ you.

It's a broken janky mess that, I'm sure, will be fantastic in about 10 years from now. Right now, though? I'd be annoyed if I had only paid CA$5 for this, but pissed that I paid CA$20. (I'm normally a superfan of SplattercatGaming, but I really feel he misrepresented this one as being so much way better than it actually is)

items.text:
Before I say anything else, I would like to praise the game for having a depth and complexity of systems that has given me 50+ hours of game time, most of which were enjoyable, so the game receives high marks for that alone and its worth the price of admission.

Having said that, having invested 50+ hours of time into the game at the time of writing this, I've both seen and discovered through experimentation the limits of the game that has been developed so far, and I find myself frustrated with the constraints of what's been sorely overlooked and what clearly hasn't yet been finished.

The game implies and promises an open world with a diverse set of playstyles, but as things currently stand, the game is really only fully developed around one gameplay loop of one particular style of gameplay and not much else at the time of this review.

The core gameplay loop involves flying out to derelict vessels in the small system you start the game out in, boarding broken and abandoned ships and then salvaging any valuable loot or in-tact systems like reactors and fuel, fighting the ocassional pirate, then repairing, restoring, and selling those systems/loot on at station kiosks or the black market to steadily increase your bank account, allowing you to improve your ship and eventually earning enough to buy a bigger one, which in turn lets you haul more and more stuff on each of your salvaging trips.

There are, however, a few fundamental problems with this gameplay loop that'll eventually leave wanting wanting to stray from the formula, and the moment you do, you really start to see the glaring gaps in design and development not yet finished.

For starters, the vast, vast majority of ships you have access to at the start are very small, yet also very expensive.

You need a certain amount of space to make sure all your vital systems have room to be installed and maintained. This includes anything from your Nav console where you actually pilot the ship to the fuel canisters and intake valves you'll need to run the thrusters, the oxygen tank that gives life support, heating and cooling systems to keep the cabin conditions livable without an exo-suit, the transponder which is how the game handles your ship ID, ship batteries, and a number of alarm systems and wiring that strings it all together.

You need all of this to operate, AND you also need as much cabin space as possible to load the often very large and very cumbersome pieces of tech you strip from the other, bigger ships.

It won't be long before you realize you'll need a bigger ship to earn more money, but you'll quickly run into a fundamental problem in that, even on the blackmarket, in perfect restored condition, you are only ever going to earn $20,000 - $80,000 for the big items you take off the derelicts, of which you'll be lucky to fit only one or two onto your small starting ship.

The second issue you'll encounter is that, even with fast forward capabilities, everything takes a very, very long time to actually accomplish. Everything from uninstalling a componenet, to repairing it, to then restoring it, takes a lot of in-game time that can take minutes on end even at x16 speed, and that in itself is nothing compared to the tediousness of space travel and having to manually operate the docking and undocking procedure every time you need to land to travel anywhere.

The process of leaving the starting port, traveling to a derelict, docking there, stripping it for parts, traveling back to and docking at the port, repairing everything that's broken, then restoring everything to perfect condition for sale, even at high speeds, can often take you anywhere from 45 minutes to over an hour of IRL time, all for what amounts to only $80,000 - $120,000 of in-game currency.

This is not an economical use of time, especially when other expenses also chip away at your earnings, like constant docking fees and refueling needs for power, fuel, and oxygen, as well as a mortgage payment that kicks in every in-game shift and penalizes you with late fees if you forget to pay.

As it turns out, you don't even own the vessel you start out with, you have to pay off an expensive mortgage that ranges anywhere from $300,000 to over $2M depending on the vessel you wind up with in the beginning, so by the time you're feeling the inadequacies of your starting vessel not only do you not have any money to invest into buying a new one, but you have a mortage to pay off before you can even think about getting a new ship.

Even when you're stripping out valuable reactors and rare intake thrusters from giant derelicts, you will be playing most of the game in debt.

After the gameplay loop gets boring after awhile, this is where you'll be tempted into expanding into the other avenues of gameplay the game seems to offer, like paid delivery quests or even piracy, but sadly these are underdeveloped or not implemented at all.

As to quests, you'll contacted all the time with a hundred different quests that all sound interesting, but the trouble is there's no real way to track where any of them are. Certain NPCs on the port you start in will have some simple social quests to accomplish, but beyond that, the vast majority of the quests your receive both at random and at the "gig board" in the station wind up going to places that are currently inaccessible.

Many times the NPCs you need to talk to are on another vessel somewhere in space, with no real way of tracking where that vessel is where it's going. The rest of the time, you'll see lots of quests based in larger and different spaceports, but as things are in the game currently, you have absolutely no way to reach them.

All the ship systems that are currently in the game are, so far, designed only to travel around the small starting area. Other systems DO exist, but they are so so far away that no ship battery or fuel system currently exists that has the speed or longevity to reach them. With most current ship systems you have, at most, a few in-game days of power and fuel to travel.

The other systems are SO FAR away that even if you use all your fuel to max out your ship speed on normal thrusters, it will take you over a in-game year to reach your destination. Even if you magically could make sure your fuel never runs out and your batteries never die, your character has food, drink, and sleep gauges that need to be constantly micromanaged.

With salvaging parts taking too much time for not much money, and with the lucrative quest system mostly broken, you're not left with many legitimate ways to earn real money to buy better ships, so this is where you might start flirting with the idea of playing the game more like a pirate.

This IS fun for awhile, and raiding the smaller stations in the starting area's perimeter as well as patrol vessels turns out to be more of a guarantee of good loot than the random junk you can often wind up with docking with derelicts, but you still suffer from a lack of cargo space and its ultimately not any more time effective than salvaging.

This is where you might get the idea to start stealing patrol ships or finding larger derelicts and patching them up and taking them for yourself, but for me, this is where the game completely fell apart.

This is due to the biggest and most frustrating aspect about the entire game, and that's the ship registration and transponder system.

Everything your ship does, from paying your mortgage to docking at ports, is dependent on your Transponder ID.

If you uninstall your transponder it has an 80% chance to break, meaning you can't even dock at the home port anymore.
Even if you DO successfully uninstall it, it cannot be placed anywhere except your starting ship.
If you put it in a derelict you've repaired to working order? It doesn't work, put in a stolen patrol ship? Doesn't work.

This means there's no real way to have a ship other than buying one, so playing as a pirate? Not possible.

Very fun, but not finished.

在我开始说其他任何事情之前，我想先赞扬这款游戏，它拥有深度和复杂性的系统，给了我50多个小时的游戏时间，其中大部分时间都很愉快，所以仅凭这一点，这款游戏就获得了很高的评价，而且它的票价是值得的。

话虽如此，在撰写本文时，我已经在这款游戏上投入了50多个小时，我既看到了也通过实验发现了迄今为止所开发游戏的局限性，我发现自己对严重被忽视和明显尚未完成的内容的限制感到沮丧。

这款游戏暗示并承诺了一个拥有多样化玩法的开放世界，但就目前情况而言，在撰写这篇评测时，游戏实际上只围绕一种特定游戏风格的一个玩法循环进行了充分开发，除此之外别无其他。

核心玩法循环包括：飞往你开始游戏时所在的小星系中的废弃船只，登上破损和废弃的飞船，然后打捞任何有价值的战利品或完好的系统，如反应堆和燃料，偶尔与海盗战斗，然后在空间站售货亭或黑市上修理、恢复和出售这些系统/战利品，以稳步增加你的银行账户，让你能够改进你的飞船，并最终赚到足够的钱买一艘更大的飞船，这反过来又让你在每次打捞之旅中运送越来越多的东西。

然而，这个玩法循环存在一些根本性问题，最终会让你想要偏离这个公式，而当你这样做的那一刻，你真的开始看到设计和开发中尚未完成的明显空白。

首先，你在开始时可以使用的绝大多数飞船都非常小，但也非常昂贵。

你需要一定的空间来确保所有重要系统都有安装和维护的空间。这包括从你实际驾驶飞船的导航控制台，到运行推进器所需的燃料罐和进气阀，提供生命支持的氧气罐，使舱内条件在没有外骨骼服的情况下也能居住的加热和冷却系统，游戏用来处理你飞船ID的应答器，飞船电池，以及将这一切连接起来的若干警报系统和线路。

你需要所有这些才能运作，而且你还需要尽可能多的舱内空间来装载你从其他更大飞船上拆下的通常非常大且非常笨重的技术部件。

不久你就会意识到你需要一艘更大的飞船来赚更多的钱，但你很快就会遇到一个根本性问题：即使是在黑市上，以完美修复的状态，你从废弃船只上拆下的大件物品也只能卖到20,000到80,000美元，而你的小型起始飞船能装下一两个就算幸运了。

你会遇到的第二个问题是，即使有快进功能，一切实际上都需要非常非常长的时间才能完成。从卸载一个组件，到修理它，再到恢复它，都需要大量的游戏内时间，即使以16倍速度也可能需要连续几分钟，而这本身与太空旅行的乏味以及每次需要着陆前往任何地方时都必须手动操作对接和脱离对接程序相比，根本不算什么。

离开起始港口、前往废弃船只、在那里对接、拆解零件、返回
停靠到港口，修理所有损坏的东西，然后把一切恢复到完美状态以便出售，即使以高速进行，通常也会花费你45分钟到超过一个小时的现实时间，而这一切只换来相当于游戏内货币80,000到120,000美元的收入。

这不是对时间的划算利用，尤其是当其他开支也在蚕食你的收入时，比如持续的停靠费和为电力、燃料和氧气补给的需求，以及每个游戏内班次都会触发的抵押贷款还款，如果你忘记支付还会被处以滞纳金。

事实证明，你甚至并不拥有你一开始的那艘船，你必须偿还一笔昂贵的抵押贷款，金额从300,000美元到超过200万美元不等，取决于你一开始得到的是哪艘船，所以等到你感受到起始船只的不足时，你不仅没有任何钱可以投资购买新船，而且在你能考虑买新船之前还有一笔抵押贷款要还清。

即使你从巨大的废弃船只上拆下宝贵的反应堆和稀有的进气推进器，你在游戏的大部分时间里仍会处于负债状态。

在游戏循环过了一段时间变得无聊之后，这时你会被诱惑去拓展游戏似乎提供的其他玩法途径，比如付费送货任务甚至海盗行为，但遗憾的是这些内容要么开发不足，要么根本没有实现。

至于任务，你会一直被联系，收到上百个听起来都很有趣的不同任务，但问题在于没有真正的方法来追踪它们在哪里。你起始港口上的某些NPC会有一些简单的社交任务可以完成，但除此之外，你随机收到以及在空间站“任务板”上收到的大多数任务最终都指向目前无法到达的地方。

很多时候你需要交谈的NPC在太空某处的另一艘船上，而没有真正的方法追踪那艘船在哪里、要去哪里。其余时候，你会看到很多基于更大、不同太空港的任务，但按照游戏目前的情况，你绝对没有办法到达它们。

目前游戏中所有的飞船系统，到目前为止，都只是为了在小小的起始区域周围旅行而设计的。其他星系确实存在，但它们如此如此遥远，以至于目前不存在任何飞船电池或燃料系统拥有足够的速度或续航能力到达它们。以你目前拥有的大多数飞船系统，你最多只有几个游戏日的电力和燃料可供旅行。

其他星系是如此遥远，以至于即使你用尽所有燃料、用普通推进器将飞船速度开到最大，也需要超过一个游戏年才能到达目的地。即使你能神奇地确保燃料永不耗尽、电池永不枯竭，你的角色也有食物、饮水和睡眠指标需要不断微操管理。

由于打捞零件花费太多时间却赚不了多少钱，而利润丰厚的任务系统又大部分是坏的，你没有剩下多少合法途径来赚取真正的钱去购买更好的飞船，所以这时你可能会开始动起把游戏玩得更像海盗的念头。

这在一段时间内确实有趣，突袭起始区域外围的较小空间站以及巡逻船只，结果比停靠废弃船只时经常得到的随机垃圾更能保证获得好战利品，但你仍然受困于货舱空间不足
空间，而且它最终并不比打捞更省时间。

这就是你可能会产生开始偷巡逻船或寻找更大的废弃船只、把它们修补好并据为己有的想法的地方，但对我来说，这正是游戏彻底崩溃的地方。

这是由于整个游戏最大、最令人沮丧的方面，那就是船舶注册和应答器系统。

你的船所做的一切，从偿还抵押贷款到在港口停靠，都依赖于你的应答器ID。

如果你卸载应答器，它有80%的几率损坏，这意味着你甚至不能再在母港停靠。
即使你确实成功卸载了它，它也不能被放置在任何地方，除了你的起始船只。
如果你把它放进一艘你已经修复到可工作状态的废弃船只？它不工作，放进一艘偷来的巡逻船？不工作。

这意味着除了购买一艘船之外，没有真正的方法拥有船只，所以扮演海盗？不可能。

非常有趣，但尚未完成。

items.text:
I spend a significant amount of time masturbating in my ship and watching porn during LAN parties because my need for intimacy is shockingly strong. Naturally, I'm having a great time. (Try to avoid lustful traits)

The learning curve isn't as steep as folks claim and I wouldn't say the devs inhibit success right from the gate, but the sooner you embrace failure the better - experimentation is important; however, this isn't a "dying is fun" kind of game. There's no ten hours of failure before you learn how to operate an airlock.

While I can't praise the immersive UI enough, I do wish for a more QoL regarding window placement and tracking which window belongs to which container. Some elements are far larger than they should be and it gets very messy very quickly, especially with cargo pants.

I also fear for mid- and late-game depth as distant areas seem to be more of the same, but Ostranauts is a sandbox and is what you make of it. You'll almost certainly be derelict ship harvester with the occasional detective job (don't get too excited, it's very basic) and eventually save up enough money for a home and cargo ship to shuttle bulk goods from A to B. In a nutshell, that's the game. The rest lies in immersion, roleplay, and a bit of imagination.

我在我的飞船里花大量时间自慰，并在局域网聚会期间看色情片，因为我对亲密关系的需求强得惊人。自然，我玩得很开心。（尽量避免好色的特质）

学习曲线并不像人们说的那么陡峭，我也不会说开发者从一开始就阻碍成功，但你越早接受失败越好——实验很重要；然而，这并不是那种“死亡很有趣”的游戏。不会在你学会如何操作气闸之前先让你失败十个小时。

虽然我对这个沉浸式UI怎么称赞都不为过，但我确实希望有更多关于窗口放置以及追踪哪个窗口属于哪个容器的生活质量改进。有些元素比它们应有的尺寸大得多，而且很快就会变得非常混乱，尤其是使用 cargo pants 时。

我也担心中期和后期的深度，因为远处的区域似乎大同小异，但 Ostranauts 是一个沙盒，取决于你怎么玩。你几乎肯定会成为废弃飞船打捞者，偶尔接点侦探工作（别太兴奋，那非常基础），最终攒够钱买一个家和一艘货船，把大宗货物从A运到B。简而言之，这就是这款游戏。其余的都在于沉浸感、角色扮演和一点想象力。

6.8 小時
我知道這個時長打一個差評很不負責任，即使評論區很多人說内容過少，但是我也并沒有體驗到那個地步，主要遇到了想関游戲的場景，實在不解
1 慢節奏游戲我其實很喜歡，但并不認爲其要繁瑣，物品欄我真的好好找有沒有固定按鈕了，每次esc就重置位置，很多物品欄也佔位置，撿垃圾的游戲居然能讓我覺得把東西拖進背包裏是很麻煩的事情，本身就能證明ui設計的不足，還有時間的ui設置，我需要頻繁的調整流速，做事情很需要時間，做完事情不能回調到初始的一倍嗎？（我真的很新人，是不是一些東西藏設置裏頭了？）
2我開局偷了個鑰匙開的船，很幸運撿了個貨船，回去賣了一波，我覺得船好小啊，那個貨船真好有船墻，我就想拆了擴建自己的船，我有工具有eva有電有時間，但是建一個火柴盒都相當麻煩，我需要一個一個拖，一個一個點，而且相當累，於是我関游戲了（別告訴我有什麽辦法可以快速建造，只怪他沒有中文）
3所以比起内容方面，我很擔心操作設計，爲什麽評論都沒有提到，真的是我不看新手教程的原因嗎qwq

14.2 小時有感
1除了操作蹩脚以外，我很慶幸自己沒有債務，因爲私自改船真的很便宜，而買一艘成品船不僅貴而且不實用，一口n2一個發動機，一個電池一個座駕，一套eva，已經完事了，剩下的全部來自廢船的遺產，游戲性和其經濟和蘇聯一樣獨特呢，24個小時我能搜二十條船，5000塊不過多拆兩個氧氣罐，
2經濟不行其游戲性其實也很少，除了造船外，真就一點東西沒有了，任務我是做的稀里糊塗（找不到人），戰鬥我以爲會變成回合制但沒有，我看不到海盜的血量，我只知道我徒手把他的eva撕破了，艦船武器更是沒影，搜來搜去就那麽點東西，氧氣罐甚至沒有大一號的那種，電量的消耗也稀里糊塗，eva真超模吧，一點錢幾乎永久解決三大問題，人物那麽多的特性真的有用？
3劇情不夠可以寫，任務太少可以加，但一些底層邏輯，我還是認爲...起碼我持悲觀態度，一艘船真的不能有二樓嗎，人物幾乎沒有所謂成長，時間以秒為單位那（几）十天直接從負債小子變成百萬富翁，物品的稀少帶來的則是船不能升級（還是我沒遇到高級物品？），小時候是吸一口氧氣，長大了那無非加給氧氣罐，電池那一塊塊加上，發動機一個一個安，從木棒打黃牛到十個木棒打十頭黃牛，連金箍棒打牛魔王都不算，
4明年怎麽敢1.0的，這個進度實在不敢恭維，我玩末日拾荒者的時候，最後感到了虎頭蛇尾，但很快釋然了，起碼由頭有尾，人物從玻璃刀到散彈槍，途中則是打人打狗，吃野果搜危房，好有感覺，地圖雖然很有限但很有意思，畢竟，是個很老的游戲了，但現在都2024年了，我電腦換了三遍了，爲什麽做出末日拾荒者的團隊只能端出這麽半成品都不是的殘疾游戲的，復古不是尸僵，硬核不是硬套 ，情懷不是濾鏡

9/10 分游戏。
下次我要装一个二氧化碳泵，以免我的角色二氧化碳中毒、昏过去，然后撞上一艘正在试图调查我“所谓”非法打捞行为的巡逻船。
只给 9/10 是因为它仍处于抢先体验阶段，而且除了打捞之外还没有多少工作可做。

items.text:
I am very, very annoyed with the direction this EA is going. 
[list]
[*] UI is bad and there seems to be no efforts to improve it.
[*] Graphics is bad - dark, cluttered spaces that make your eyes hurt - and it becomes worse.
[*] Social interactions - I outright hate those, 20 different lines clutter aforementioned bad UI and maybe 3 of them are useful.
[*] Quests are random generated pointless nonsence, and in latest version you are bombarded by them
[*] No adequate starmap, local maps, general derelict plans etc. 
[/list]
Game is bad at telling you what happens around you, what happens with you and very, very bad at telling you what your are supposed to do.

It's playable, yes, and there are [i]some[/i] imporvement but it was to pain to play back in 2020 and is pain to play now.

IDK, maybe I'll check in another 2 to 4 years. But for now I better play again NEO Scavenger again, at least THAT game was able to explain that I am in pain because of wearing a left shoe on the right leg...
items.text_zh:
我对这个EA游戏的发展方向感到非常、非常恼火。
[list]
[*] UI很糟糕，而且似乎没有任何改进的努力。
[*] 画面很差——黑暗、杂乱的空间让你的眼睛疼——而且还在变得更糟。
[*] 社交互动——我彻底讨厌这些，20条不同的台词塞满了上述糟糕的UI，也许其中3条有用。
[*] 任务是随机生成的无意义废话，而在最新版本中你被它们狂轰滥炸
[*] 没有合适的星图、本地地图、一般的废弃飞船平面图等。
[/list]
游戏很不擅长告诉你周围发生了什么、你身上发生了什么，而且非常、非常不擅长告诉你应该做什么。

它是可玩的，是的，而且有[i]一些[/i]改进，但在2020年玩起来很痛苦，现在玩起来也很痛苦。

不知道，也许再过2到4年我会再看看。但就目前而言，我宁愿再玩一次NEO Scavenger，至少那个游戏能够解释我因为把左脚的鞋穿在右脚上而感到疼痛……
